Provisions for the September quarter stood at ₹1,694 crore, down from ₹2,223 crore in the June quarter and ₹3,547 crore in the year-ago period. The Bank holds cumulative provisions (standard + additional other than NPA) of ₹15,860 crores as on September 30, 2026.
It is pertinent to note that this is over and above the NPA provisioning included in the Bank’s PCR calculations.
Axis Bank acquired around 1.09 million cards in Q2FY27, with its market share at approximately 13.1% of cards in force.

The bank’s gross slippage ratio stood at 1.48%, down 63 basis points year-on-year and 31 basis points quarter-on-quarter, while the net slippage ratio declined 30 basis points year-on-year and 37 basis points sequentially to 0.75%. Fresh slippages fell to ₹4,762 crore from ₹5,566 crore in the previous quarter, while upgradations and recoveries rose to ₹2,380 crore from ₹2,126 crore sequentially.

Loans extended by the bank's international branches to customers as leveraging facility stood at $4.57 billion, and adjusted for these loans, Axis Bank's gross advances would have grown by 17% from last year, and 2.6% sequentially, while deposits would have grown by 17% year-on-year and 2.6% from the June quarter.
Axis Bank also issued standby letters of credit to other lenders in respect to loans against FCNR (B) deposits. That amount stood at $4.69 billion.

Shares of Axis Bank ended little changed ahead of the results announcement at ₹1,290. The stock is up 4% in the last one month and is barely managing to stay above the flat line on a year-to-date basis.

title: Axis Bank Q2 Results: Core Income beats; Asset Quality, slippages better sequentially
